title: The Holy Spirit
summary: Who the Holy Spirit is and what He does: in creation, in Scripture, in Christ, in salvation and in the believer's life.
description: The Holy Spirit is often misunderstood: treated as a force, an emotion, or a power to be used. This course shows from Scripture that He is the third Person of the Trinity, fully God, and traces His work in creation, in inspiring Scripture, in the life of Jesus, in conviction and new birth, in the believer's holiness and fruit, and in equipping the church for witness and service.
objectives: Establish the personhood and deity of the Holy Spirit
Trace the Spirit's work in the Old Testament and in Christ
Explain His work in salvation: conviction, regeneration, indwelling and sealing
Explain His work in sanctification, fruit and empowering for service
outcomes: Show the Spirit is a Person and is God
Describe His role in creation, prophecy and the life of Jesus
Name the fruit of the Spirit and explain walking in the Spirit
Describe the Spirit's empowering for witness

modules.title: Who Is the Holy Spirit?
modules.intro: This week we see that the Holy Spirit is not an 'it' but 'He': a divine Person, equal with the Father and the Son.

lessons.title: A Person, not a power
lessons.body:
Jesus spoke of the Spirit as "he": "when he, the Spirit of truth, is come, he will guide you into all truth" (John 16:13). Though the Greek word for spirit is neuter, John uses a masculine pronoun deliberately.

The Spirit does what persons do. He teaches (John 14:26), testifies (John 15:26), speaks (Acts 13:2), forbids (Acts 16:6-7), intercedes (Romans 8:26) and distributes gifts "as he will" (1 Corinthians 12:11). He can be lied to (Acts 5:3), grieved (Ephesians 4:30), resisted (Acts 7:51) and blasphemed (Matthew 12:31).

We do not use the Spirit; He leads us.

lessons.title: The Spirit is God
lessons.body:
Peter equates lying to the Holy Ghost with lying to God (Acts 5:3-4). The Spirit has divine attributes: He is eternal (Hebrews 9:14), everywhere present (Psalm 139:7-8), all-knowing (1 Corinthians 2:10-11) and the giver of life (Romans 8:11).

He is named alongside the Father and Son as equal: in baptism (Matthew 28:19) and the apostolic blessing (2 Corinthians 13:14).

The Nicene Creed confesses Him as "the Lord, the giver of life", worshipped and glorified together with the Father and the Son.

lessons.title: Names and symbols
lessons.body:
The Spirit's names reveal His work: the **Holy** Spirit (His character), the **Spirit of truth** (John 14:17), the **Comforter** or helper (John 14:16), the **Spirit of adoption** (Romans 8:15), the **Spirit of Christ** (Romans 8:9), the **Spirit of grace** (Hebrews 10:29).

Scripture also uses symbols: **wind** or breath (John 3:8; Acts 2:2), **fire** (Acts 2:3), **water** (John 7:38-39), **oil** for anointing (1 John 2:20), a **dove** (Matthew 3:16) and a **seal** (Ephesians 1:13).

Symbols help us understand, but they must not reduce Him to an impersonal force.

terms.def: The third Person of the Trinity, fully God.
Greek parakletos: one called alongside to help, counsel and encourage.
Jesus' title for the Spirit who guides into all truth.
To sadden the Holy Spirit by sin (Ephesians 4:30).
Deliberately attributing the Spirit's work in Christ to Satan (Matthew 12:31-32).
The Spirit's presence equipping a person for God's service, pictured by oil.

texts.teaches: The Spirit of truth will guide believers into all truth.
Lying to the Holy Ghost is lying to God.
Grieve not the Holy Spirit of God.
The Spirit searches the deep things of God.
The Father will give another Comforter to abide for ever.

summary: The Holy Spirit is a Person: He teaches, speaks, intercedes and can be grieved.
He is fully God, equal with the Father and the Son.
His names show His holiness, truth and help.
Symbols such as wind, fire, water, oil and dove illustrate His work.

questions.q: Which pronoun did Jesus use for the Spirit in John 16:13?
What does "Comforter" mean?
Which shows the Spirit is a Person?
Which symbol of the Spirit appeared at Jesus' baptism?

modules.title: The Spirit in the Old Testament and in Christ
modules.intro: The Spirit was active from creation, inspired the prophets and filled Jesus. This week we trace His work before Pentecost.

lessons.title: Creation, prophets and leaders
lessons.body:
At creation "the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters" (Genesis 1:2). He gives life: "thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created" (Psalm 104:30).

In the Old Testament the Spirit came upon particular people for particular tasks: Bezaleel for craftsmanship (Exodus 31:3), judges such as Gideon (Judges 6:34), kings such as David (1 Samuel 16:13), and the prophets, who spoke "as they were moved by the Holy Ghost" (2 Peter 1:21).

This presence could be withdrawn, as with Saul (1 Samuel 16:14); David prayed, "take not thy holy spirit from me" (Psalm 51:11).

lessons.title: The promise of the Spirit
lessons.body:
The prophets promised a new age of the Spirit. Moses wished "that all the LORD's people were prophets" (Numbers 11:29). Ezekiel: "I will put my spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes" (Ezekiel 36:27). Joel: "I will pour out my spirit upon all flesh" (Joel 2:28).

John the Baptist said the coming One would "baptize you with the Holy Ghost, and with fire" (Matthew 3:11). Jesus promised the Spirit would be "in" His disciples, not only "with" them (John 14:17), after He was glorified (John 7:39).

lessons.title: The Spirit in the life of Jesus
lessons.body:
The Spirit was at work at every stage of Jesus' life. He was conceived by the Holy Ghost (Luke 1:35). At His baptism the Spirit descended on Him (Luke 3:22). "Full of the Holy Ghost" He was led into the wilderness (Luke 4:1) and returned "in the power of the Spirit" (4:14).

He announced, "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he hath anointed me to preach the gospel" (Luke 4:18). He cast out devils "by the Spirit of God" (Matthew 12:28), offered Himself "through the eternal Spirit" (Hebrews 9:14), and was raised by the Spirit (Romans 8:11).

The same Spirit now dwells in believers.

terms.def: The Old Testament name for the Holy Spirit, active from creation.
The Spirit's empowering of particular people for tasks in the Old Testament.
The promised giving of the Spirit to all God's people.
Jesus' contrast between the Spirit's presence before and after Pentecost (John 14:17).
John's description of Christ's work of pouring out the Spirit.
The Spirit through whom Christ offered Himself (Hebrews 9:14).

texts.teaches: The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
God will put His Spirit within His people to make them obey.
God will pour out His Spirit upon all flesh.
The Spirit of the Lord anointed Jesus to preach the gospel.
Jesus cast out devils by the Spirit of God.

summary: The Spirit worked in creation and gives life.
In the Old Testament He came upon leaders and prophets for tasks.
The prophets promised He would be poured out on all God's people.
Jesus was conceived, anointed, led and empowered by the Spirit.

questions.q: Whom did the Spirit fill for craftsmanship in Exodus 31?
Which prophet promised the Spirit poured out on all flesh?
In which synagogue sermon did Jesus say "The Spirit of the Lord is upon me"?
What did David pray in Psalm 51:11?
options: Take not thy holy spirit from me

modules.title: The Spirit in Salvation
modules.intro: Salvation is the Spirit's work from start to finish. This week: conviction, new birth, indwelling, sealing and assurance.

lessons.title: Conviction and new birth
lessons.body:
Jesus said the Spirit "will reprove the world of sin, and of righteousness, and of judgment" (John 16:8). He opens eyes to see our sin and Christ's sufficiency.

He also gives new life. "Except a man be born of water and of the Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God" (John 3:5). This is **regeneration**: God "saved us, by the washing of regeneration, and renewing of the Holy Ghost" (Titus 3:5).

New birth is God's work, like the wind that blows where it wills (John 3:8). It results in faith, repentance and a changed life.

lessons.title: Indwelling and sealing
lessons.body:
Every true believer has the Holy Spirit living within: "if any man have not the Spirit of Christ, he is none of his" (Romans 8:9). Our bodies are His temple (1 Corinthians 6:19).

Believers are "sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance" (Ephesians 1:13-14). A **seal** marks ownership and security; an **earnest** is a down payment guaranteeing full payment later.

The Spirit also unites believers with Christ and with one another: "by one Spirit are we all baptized into one body" (1 Corinthians 12:13).

lessons.title: Adoption and assurance
lessons.body:
The Spirit makes us aware that we belong to God. "Ye have received the Spirit of adoption, whereby we cry, Abba, Father. The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God" (Romans 8:15-16).

This witness is not only a feeling. It works with the evidence of a changed life: love for God's people (1 John 3:14), obedience (1 John 2:3) and the fruit of the Spirit.

The Spirit also helps us pray: "the Spirit itself maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered" (Romans 8:26).

terms.def: The Spirit's work of showing people their sin and need of Christ.
The new birth: the Spirit giving new spiritual life.
The Spirit's permanent presence within every believer.
The Spirit marking believers as God's possession and securing them.
A down payment guaranteeing the rest; the Spirit as pledge of our inheritance.
The Spirit who assures believers they are God's children.

texts.teaches: The Spirit convicts the world of sin, righteousness and judgement.
A person must be born of water and of the Spirit to enter God's kingdom.
Anyone without the Spirit of Christ is not His.
Believers are sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise.
The Spirit bears witness with our spirit that we are God's children.

summary: The Spirit convicts of sin and gives new birth.
He indwells every believer and seals them as God's own.
He unites believers to Christ and to His body.
He assures us we are God's children and helps us pray.

questions.q: What is regeneration?
options: The new birth by the Spirit

questions.q: According to Romans 8:9, who belongs to Christ?
options: Those who have the Spirit of Christ

questions.q: What is an "earnest" in Ephesians 1:14?
options: A down payment guaranteeing the rest

questions.q: What does the Spirit of adoption enable us to cry?

modules.title: Walking in the Spirit
modules.intro: The Spirit makes believers holy and fruitful. This week we study the fruit of the Spirit and how to walk in step with Him.

lessons.title: Flesh and Spirit
lessons.body:
Believers experience a conflict: "the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh" (Galatians 5:17). The *flesh* here means our sinful nature, not the body.

The answer is not mere willpower: "Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh" (Galatians 5:16). "If ye through the Spirit do mortify the deeds of the body, ye shall live" (Romans 8:13).

The works of the flesh are plain: immorality, idolatry, witchcraft, hatred, strife, envy, drunkenness and the like (Galatians 5:19-21).

lessons.title: The fruit of the Spirit
lessons.body:
"But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance" (Galatians 5:22-23).

Note that it is *fruit*, singular: one harvest of Christlike character with nine flavours. Fruit grows; it is not manufactured. It comes from abiding in Christ (John 15:4-5).

Gifts show what the Spirit does *through* us; fruit shows what He does *in* us. Jesus said, "by their fruits ye shall know them" (Matthew 7:20). Character, not only power, is the mark of a Spirit-filled life.

lessons.title: Be filled with the Spirit
lessons.body:
Paul commands, "be not drunk with wine... but be filled with the Spirit" (Ephesians 5:18). The tense means "keep on being filled": a continuing yielding to His control.

The results are worship, thanksgiving and humble relationships in the home and church (5:19-6:9).

We can **grieve** the Spirit by sin (Ephesians 4:30) and **quench** Him by resisting His work (1 Thessalonians 5:19). We walk in step with Him by confessing sin, obeying the Word, praying, and yielding daily to His leading (Romans 8:14).

terms.def: In Paul's letters, the sinful nature opposed to God.
Living daily under the Spirit's guidance and power.
The Christlike character the Spirit produces, listed in Galatians 5:22-23.
To put to death the deeds of the sinful nature.
Continually yielded to and controlled by the Holy Spirit.
To resist or stifle the Spirit's work.

texts.teaches: Walk in the Spirit and you will not fulfil the lust of the flesh.
The Spirit produces love, joy, peace and other Christlike fruit.
Through the Spirit, put to death the deeds of the body and live.
Be filled with the Spirit, not drunk with wine.
Quench not the Spirit.

summary: The flesh and the Spirit are in conflict in the believer.
We overcome the flesh by walking in the Spirit.
The fruit of the Spirit is Christlike character that grows by abiding in Christ.
Keep on being filled; do not grieve or quench the Spirit.

questions.q: How many qualities are listed in the fruit of the Spirit?
What does "flesh" mean in Galatians 5?
What is the difference between gifts and fruit?
options: Gifts show what the Spirit does through us; fruit, what He does in us

questions.q: Which verse commands believers to be filled with the Spirit?

modules.title: Power for Witness and Service
modules.intro: The Spirit equips the church to witness and serve. This week we introduce His empowering and gifts; a later course studies them in depth.

lessons.title: Ye shall receive power
lessons.body:
Before His ascension Jesus promised, "ye shall receive power, after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you: and ye shall be witnesses unto me" (Acts 1:8). At Pentecost the Spirit came, and fearful disciples became bold preachers (Acts 2:4, 14).

The early church kept praying and "they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they spake the word of God with boldness" (Acts 4:31).

The Spirit's power is given chiefly for witness: to glorify Christ (John 16:14) and spread the gospel, not for personal display or gain (Acts 8:18-21).

lessons.title: Gifts for the common good
lessons.body:
The Spirit gives every believer gifts for serving the church: "the manifestation of the Spirit is given to every man to profit withal" (1 Corinthians 12:7).

Paul lists gifts such as wisdom, knowledge, faith, healing, miracles, prophecy, discerning of spirits, tongues and interpretation (1 Corinthians 12:8-10), and also teaching, giving, leading and showing mercy (Romans 12:6-8).

Gifts must be exercised in love (1 Corinthians 13), with order (14:40), for building up others. No gift makes one believer superior to another.

lessons.title: Where Christians differ
lessons.body:
Believers agree the Spirit indwells every Christian and empowers the church. They differ on some questions, which the course *Baptism in the Spirit and Spiritual Gifts* studies fully:

- **Is the baptism in the Spirit a second experience after conversion, with speaking in tongues as initial evidence?** Pentecostal and Holiness churches, including Deeper Life, generally say yes. Most Baptists say every believer is baptized by the Spirit at conversion, with later fillings.
- **Do all spiritual gifts continue today?** Continuationists say yes; cessationists believe some sign gifts ended with the apostles.

Both sides seek to honour Scripture, and both prize holiness, love and witness.

terms.def: The Spirit's enabling for bold witness and service.
An ability given by the Spirit for serving and building up the church.
A visible working of the Spirit through a believer for the good of others.
The view that all spiritual gifts continue today.
The view that some sign gifts ceased with the apostolic age.
The Pentecostal teaching that speaking in tongues is the first sign of Spirit baptism.

texts.teaches: Believers receive power when the Holy Ghost comes, to be Christ's witnesses.
Filled with the Holy Ghost, believers spoke God's word with boldness.
The Spirit glorifies Christ.
The Spirit's manifestation is given to each for the profit of all.
The Spirit distributes gifts to each as He wills.

summary: The Spirit empowers believers to be bold witnesses for Christ.
He gives every believer gifts for the common good.
Gifts must be used in love, with order, to build others up.
Christians differ on Spirit baptism and the continuation of gifts, but all prize holiness and witness.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the power promised in Acts 1:8?
According to 1 Corinthians 12:7, spiritual gifts are given:
Which chapter says gifts without love are nothing?
What is cessationism?
options: The view that some sign gifts ceased with the apostles
The view that all gifts continue

short.q: Give three evidences that the Holy Spirit is a Person.
short.model: He teaches and speaks, can be grieved and lied to, intercedes and distributes gifts as He wills; Jesus calls Him 'He'.

short.q: How did the Spirit's work in the Old Testament differ from after Pentecost?
short.model: In the Old Testament He came upon particular people for tasks and could be withdrawn; after Pentecost He is poured out on all believers and dwells in them.
The new birth: the Holy Spirit giving new spiritual life to a sinner.

short.q: Explain sealing and the earnest of the Spirit.
short.model: The Spirit seals believers as God's possession and secure, and is the earnest, a down payment guaranteeing our future inheritance.

short.q: What is the difference between the fruit and the gifts of the Spirit?
short.model: The fruit is Christlike character the Spirit produces in us; gifts are abilities He gives for serving others through us.

short.q: Summarise the two main views on the baptism in the Spirit.
short.model: Pentecostal and Holiness churches see it as a second experience after conversion, usually evidenced by tongues; most Baptists say all believers are baptized by the Spirit at conversion, with later fillings.

lists.q: List the nine qualities of the fruit of the Spirit.
List four symbols of the Holy Spirit.
List four works of the Spirit in salvation.

assignments.title: Who is the Holy Spirit to me?
assignments.prompt: Describe how you have thought about the Holy Spirit in the past. Then, using at least five passages from this course, explain who He is and how knowing Him as a Person should change your prayer and daily life.

assignments.title: Fruit in the home
assignments.prompt: Choose three qualities from the fruit of the Spirit. For each, explain what it means, why it cannot be produced by willpower alone, and how it should show in your home, workplace or church this month.
